## What This Is

**Security fix. If you installed any version from v3.3.0 through v3.12.0, apply this update.** When your Permanent Floor gate cannot run Node, it allows every deletion and says nothing.

**If you installed v3.10.0, v3.11.0 or v3.12.0 and ran the token script, run it again after updating.** It personalized only the files inside `Council Chamber/`. Your `.claude/CLAUDE.md` still opens with "This vault is the **{{ECOSYSTEM_NAME}}**". Re-running is safe: the script only replaces tokens that are still there.

The rest of this release carries what the practice behind this template learned over seven weeks: plan alignment for code review and plan implementation, an evidence gate for the Security Check, the session end order, three new Claim Integrity faces and more. They are listed under Also in This Release. The two fixes above come first because they are the ones that matter if you read nothing else.

## The Defect

`pre-tool-approval-gate.sh` reads its payload with `node -e`. If node cannot run, the tool name comes back empty. Nothing in the file handled an empty tool name, so it fell through to the `exit 0` at the bottom. **Every `rm`, `Remove-Item` and `git rm` of a protected file passed, with no message.**

`pre-write-floor-guard.sh` had the same shape. Its one promise is that no edit to `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is ever silent. Without node it went silent.

## Why This Is Reachable Now

When the gate was written, Claude Code was installed through npm and Node came with it. That is no longer true. Claude Code's native installer and the Claude desktop app run without Node, and hooks inherit the app's environment rather than your login shell. So your terminal can print a Node version while the hook, launched by an app from a dock or a start menu, finds none. A Node installed through a version manager is the most common case: it lives on your shell's PATH and nowhere else.

The template's Quick Start installs Node first, and that path is fine. The README and Session 0 never listed Node at all.

## The Fix

When the gate cannot read its payload, it has no verdict, and a Floor guard resolves no verdict toward refusal.

- `pre-tool-approval-gate.sh` reads the tool name with a plain `grep` when node fails. For a shell tool it refuses with `FLOOR GATE INERT`, says whether node is unrunnable or the payload is unparseable, and names the fix. **Every shell call waits, including `git status`, until node is reachable again.** That is the design: a gate that cannot see the command cannot tell a deletion from a listing. Write and Edit never reach this hook and stay open.
- `pre-write-floor-guard.sh` reads `tool_name` and `file_path` with a plain `grep` when node fails, so a trust-anchor edit is still surfaced. A path that arrives JSON-escaped (`C:\\Users\\...`) is normalized before the match.

## The Specification, If You Have Customized Your Copy

Do not apply this as a patch. Your hooks may have moved. Apply the intent:

1. In `pre-tool-approval-gate.sh`, directly after the line that sets `TOOL_NAME` from node, add a branch for an empty `TOOL_NAME`. In it, extract the tool name from the raw payload with `grep -oE '"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"'`. If that name is empty, `Bash` or `PowerShell`, print a message to stderr naming the cause and the fix, then `exit 2`.
2. In `pre-write-floor-guard.sh`, when `TOOL_NAME` comes back empty, take `tool_name` and `file_path` from the raw payload the same way, and squeeze runs of slashes (`tr -s '/'`) after converting backslashes.
3. If you added other hooks that parse with node and make a decision, give each the same question: what does this hook do when node cannot run? A guard that allows on silence has a hole. A surfacing hook that goes quiet has broken its promise.

## The Test That Proves It

`floor-gate-selftest.mjs` places a `node` that cannot start first on PATH and fires three cases: a Bash `rm`, a PowerShell `Remove-Item` and a plain `git status`. All three must refuse. It also confirms the planted `node` actually won the lookup, and fails the run if it did not, because a degraded case that silently used the real node would pass for the wrong reason.

`hooks-selftest.mjs` gains two cases: with node unrunnable, the floor guard still surfaces a trust-anchor edit, for a forward-slash path and for a JSON-escaped backslash path.

**Run both before you apply the fix as well as after.** On an unpatched copy the gate self-test reports three holes and the hooks self-test reports two silent cases. On a patched copy both are green, and the hooks negative control still falsifies every case.

```sh
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/floor-gate-selftest.mjs"
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs"
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs" --negative-control
```

## Six Scripts Aimed One Folder Too Low

In v3.10.0 the scripts folder moved from the vault root into `Council Chamber/scripts/`. Six scripts kept finding the vault as the parent of their own folder, which is now `Council Chamber/`. None of them crashed. Each reported a confident result about the wrong place.

| Script | What it did | What it reported |
|---|---|---|
| `replace-tokens.mjs` | Personalized only `Council Chamber/`. The trust anchor, the Codex adapter, `AGENTS.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md` and the Getting Started sessions kept their tokens | Success |
| `doctrine-mass.mjs` | Counted nothing | Zero artifacts in every layer, exit 0 |
| `doctrine-references.mjs` | Scanned `Council Chamber/Council Chamber/` | Zero orphans, zero index-only, zero low-inbound |
| `external-worker.mjs` | Wrote its dispatch log under `Council Chamber/.runtime/` | Success |
| `se-update.mjs` | Computed paths relative to `Council Chamber/` | Success |
| `session-coordination.mjs` | Kept session state under `Council Chamber/.runtime/` | Success |

All six now resolve the vault two levels above the script. `replace-tokens.mjs` also skips `.github/`, so it no longer rewrites the release history that describes the tokens.

**A count of nothing is a wrong root, never a clean vault.** `doctrine-mass.mjs` and `doctrine-references.mjs` now exit 1 when they find no doctrine at all, and CI fires them both ways: they must find doctrine on a fresh checkout and must fail when aimed at an empty folder. The doctrine counter on this repo moves from 0 artifacts to 92, and the reference counter from 0 orphans to 27. Those 27 are the template's real state, and yours to read.

`replace-tokens-selftest.mjs` is new. It drives the token script on a throwaway copy of your vault and requires two things: answering YES leaves no identity token anywhere, including `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and answering anything else writes nothing. On the v3.12.0 script it fails on exactly the files listed above.

**If you have customized these scripts,** the specification is one line each: the vault root is the directory two levels above `Council Chamber/scripts/`. Then run each script and confirm it reports real numbers. A zero is the symptom.

## Two Scripts That Wrote When They Should Have Refused

`decision-journal.mjs` and `build-skills-index.mjs` tested their flags with `includes`, so a mistyped `--chek` ran the write path instead of the check. The journal restamped its generated date on a typo. Both now refuse an unknown argument with exit 2.

## Install and CI

- **`README.md` lists five things you need, and Node.js is one of them.** It also drops the old claim that Claude Code runs on metered API billing at $10 to $25 for onboarding. Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher) or API credits, which the Quick Start Guide has said since v3.9.0.
- **Session 0 lists Node.js** in What You Need and in its checklist.
- **CI fires the guards on Node 22 and Node 24**, both active LTS lines, since a Sovereign who follows Session 0 today installs 24. `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` move from v5 to v7.

## Also in This Release

What the practice behind this template learned over seven weeks, written in this template's own voice. Every item is additive. Your customized copies of these files can take the intent without taking the text.

### Law in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`

- **Claim Integrity gains four faces.** Reporting: label a finding by what you observed, never by its inferred cause. Carried items: every open loop records its own done-check, verdicts are open, resolved or unverifiable, and a carried item's stated scope expires with it. Absence: nothing observed from inside a running system proves absence, so a clean report names its instrument. Attribution: your words go inside quotation marks with their source, the AI interface's summary stays outside them.
- **An existence check on every "create" step.** A plan step that creates an account, repo or resource first checks that it does not already exist.
- **Dependency order over invented dates.** A date reaches a plan only when you stated it or an outside deadline imposes it.
- **Reporting to the Sovereign:** what was done, then decisions, then actions. The separation is binding, the headings are not.
- **The session end order:** finish, report with decisions, wait for your rulings, close once, then a continuation prompt when work continues.
- **Skills Location** now points at `link-skills.mjs` instead of teaching `mklink` as Administrator.

### Skills

- **PR Code Review gains Lens 6, plan alignment.** When a Pending Plan governs the change, a sixth reviewer asks whether the code is the code the plan authorized: a departure, unimplemented scope, an unplanned addition or a justified improvement. It never runs without a plan, and it quotes both sides before it claims anything.
- **Pending Plan Implementation** records the starting commit and runs a fresh-agent plan-alignment check before closing. The orchestrator never checks its own work.
- **Security Check stops laundering consensus into severity.** Agreement between passes used to elevate a finding on its own. A new verification step checks each finding against live state first, and a finding elevates only when at least one contributing pass survived it. The adversarial pass runs at Sonnet.
- **Session Closeout** gains Action 0, no close while a raised decision is open, and Action 4, the continuation prompt.
- **Self-Healing** confirms the fix worked before moving on. A fix applied is not a fix verified. Recurring errors get a durable record.
- **Brainstorm:** a grep locates and only a full read licenses a citation. When an idea faces a market, one of the three solutions is the scrappiest real test.
- **Autonomous Improvement Session:** verify before you speak. Only strong candidates, or none. A menu is not judgment. Blast radius sets the explanation budget. Its autonomy Levels are named apart from the Constitution's Trust Levels. Eleven new menu items, one retired and a fallback for a denied action.
- **Manuscript Anti-AI Edit Pass** syncs to the codex it cites. It said v1.0 with 106 entries while the codex said v1.2 with 114.
- **Playwright:** "Execution context was destroyed" means a bot-challenge redirect, never an empty page.

### Codices and protocols

- **Engineering Codex:** Orchestration Mode. Inline by default, four triggers that earn a dispatch, four conditions that keep work inline and verification rigor that never varies by mode. Plus the trusted-extension failure mode: read the bytes, never the file extension.
- **Anti-AI Writing Patterns Codex v1.3:** entry 62b, Manufactured Intent. Never supply a reason for something arbitrary. It holds on every surface, internal included.
- **Challenge and Illumination Codex:** a Creation Support Posture, silence signals and a decision rule for choosing a mode.
- **Writing Style Codex:** derived copy answers to the shipped artifact, never a draft.
- **Sovereign Tech Watch:** a two-floor grounding gate, where Hold is a complete outcome, and a partial sweep never touches rows it did not sweep.
- **Watch Register:** every row carries a done-check, verdicts are three-state and a firing that asks for an edit spawns a task.
- **Interface Adapter Protocol:** Exposure Tier Mapping E0 to E4, matching the Registry it used to contradict. A pointer to a file that never shipped now points at `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the Registry, here and in the AI Interface Activation Protocol.
- **Repo Context Architecture:** the repos are the record. The tracking table that could only drift is gone.
- **Meta-Governance Audit** names its boundary with Sovereign Tech Watch. **Session Closeout Protocol** names the question closeout exists to ask. **Collaboration Archival** states that it takes precedence over Batch Archival under `Collaborations/`.
- **Doctrine mass** can leave records out: list record folders in `RECORD_DIRS`, or mark a file `doctrine: false`. Excluded counts are reported per layer.

### Not in this release, on purpose

Two refinements to the deletion gate narrow what it refuses: a relative path in a session rooted in another repo, and a deletion that is only quoted inside a commit message. Both are proven in practice. Both loosen a guard, and widening a classifier is the change most likely to open a door. They ship in a release of their own, with their must-block cases first, so a regression can be traced to one change.

## Verification

Run against a fresh clone of v3.12.0 with this release applied, `SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT` unset, Node 24:

- Floor gate self-test 32 of 32, including three node-unrunnable cases watched failing on v3.12.0 first.
- Hooks self-test 20 of 20, negative control 12 of 12 falsified.
- Token script self-test 6 of 6. On the v3.12.0 script it fails on the trust anchor and four more files.
- Doctrine mass and doctrine references each find 92 artifacts and each exit 1 on an empty root.
- Decision Journal, Skills Index, citation, mirror and linker checks green. Zero em dashes in active files, no author paths.
- CI runs the guards on Node 22 and 24.
